title: Introduce build-hash contracts and transparent layer rotation for reproducible CI outputs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our CI builds produce artifacts that can differ between runs because of non-deterministic layer ordering, transient base image updates, and language toolchain variability. This increases flakiness, bloats cache storage, and complicates artifact signing for downstream deployments.

Goal: Define a lightweight build-hash contract that guarantees deterministic artifact identity for a given source commit + build inputs, and implement a transparent layer rotation mechanism that allows us to swap base image layers (slim/secure variants) without invalidating downstream builds when the contract is satisfied. Deliverables: (1) spec for build-hash contract; (2) build profiler that records layer usage and canonicalizes layer ordering; (3) a CI-side rotation service that can rotate endorsed base-layer digests while preserving build-hash compatibility; (4) artifact signing and verification step integrated into existing release pipeline.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Contract surface: contract will include source hash, build flags, locked dependency digests (package lockfiles), and an ordered list of layer digests as canonicalized by the profiler. We avoid encoding ambient timestamps or ephemeral local paths.
- Rotation approach: rotation alters base layer digest but only if the profiler confirms identical file-level content exposed to the build (via layer content checksum). This reduces unnecessary cache bustage while enabling us to proactively switch to smaller or security-patched base layers.
- Performance: the profiler adds a lightweight post-build pass to record layer/file checksums; overhead targeted < 5% build time for large images.
- Storage: signed artifact metadata will be stored in the existing artifact bucket under /signed-manifests to avoid creating new infra services.
- Security: signatures will be generated with CI's KMS key; verification step added to Dedicated and Private deploy pipelines. Security review required before rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) Spec + tests (2 weeks): finalize contract format (RFC doc), unit tests for canonicalizer.
2) Profiler PoC (2 weeks): integrate with existing build runner for node/python images; produce canonical manifest.
3) Rotation pilot (1 week): configure rotation for a low-traffic internal runtime image; monitor cache hit ratio and build latencies.
4) Artifact signing (1 week): add sign/verify steps to release job.
5) Gradual enable (2 weeks): expand to critical image families, monitor for unexpected invalidations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repeatable builds: identical build-hash for identical inputs across 95% of trials (target 99% for stable images).
- Cache hit improvement: at least 15% reduction in full-rebuilds caused by base image churn during pilot.
- No deployment failures due to rotation in pilot cluster.
- Signed artifacts verifiable by release pipeline.

Testing & QA: Unit tests for canonicalizer, integration tests exercising rotation path, canary deploys to staging for signed artifacts, chaos test where a base layer is rotated mid-build to confirm safe fallback.

Rollback plan: Rotation changes are controlled by feature-flag; on detecting >2% increase in build failures or signature mismatches we will immediately disable rotation and revert to previous base digests.

Open questions:
- Do we need to extend package-lock capture to include OS-level packages installed in Dockerfile RUN steps? (suggest capturing checksums of apt cache layers).
- How to represent non-file system inputs (build args that influence compile outputs) in a compact way.

Related artifacts: RFC doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/build-hash-contract-rfc (internal), initial profiler PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/build-profiler/pulls/12, early metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci-builds/build-hash-metrics
